items.stem: When comparing freight options, why is 'total landed cost' preferred over the quoted freight rate alone?

options.text: It includes transport, duties, handling, inventory and other costs to the destination
options.rationale: Correct: total landed cost captures all costs of getting goods to their destination, not just freight.

options.text: It is always lower than the freight rate
options.rationale: Landed cost is typically higher because it adds more cost elements.
Landed cost specifically includes duties and customs charges.

options.text: It applies only to domestic shipments
options.rationale: Landed cost is especially relevant for international shipments.

items.explanation: Correct: total landed cost captures all costs of getting goods to their destination, not just freight.

items.stem: A shipper must move low-value, non-urgent bulk goods across an ocean at the lowest cost. Which mode best fits?

options.rationale: Correct: ocean is the lowest-cost mode for non-urgent, high-volume international cargo.
Air is fastest but far more costly, unsuited to low-value non-urgent goods.
Expedited courier is for urgent, time-critical parcels at premium cost.
Same-day local delivery cannot cross an ocean and is costly.

items.explanation: Correct: ocean is the lowest-cost mode for non-urgent, high-volume international cargo.

items.stem: Select TWO factors that raise an item's reorder point.

options.rationale: Correct: more time to replenish means ordering sooner, raising the reorder point.

options.text: Higher average demand during lead time
options.rationale: Correct: greater demand over the lead time increases the quantity needed before resupply.
A shorter lead time lowers, not raises, the reorder point.
Lower demand reduces the reorder point.
Storage cost does not change the demand-and-lead-time reorder calculation.

items.explanation: Correct: more time to replenish means ordering sooner, raising the reorder point. Correct: greater demand over the lead time increases the quantity needed before resupply.
